_about: TRACKED seed: business PHRASE -> concrete column VALUE, per source. Published into the per-source artifact veda_value_aliases.json by the L5 stage ingestion/entity_alias_seeder.py (publish_values), and consumed by query/value_glossary.py before SQL generation.
_why: A lifecycle qualifier is not a word that appears in the data. 'currently on the market for sale' means assets_salelisting.status = 'APPROVED', but no sampled value contains the words 'on the market', so the value arbiter (which grounds by EXACT value match) could not see it and the qualifier was silently dropped: the 2026-09-23 run answered 'the cheapest properties currently ON THE MARKET' with 74 of 100 rows DRAFT or CANCELLED, and the three cheapest rows were all DRAFT.
_shape: {"<table>.<column>": {"<VALUE>": [phrases...]}}. Phrases are matched case-insensitively as whole phrases against the query.
_pruned_2026_09_23: 'for sale' / 'up for sale' / 'listed' were removed: they name the ENTITY (assets_salelisting is the sale-listing table) rather than a lifecycle value, so mapping them to APPROVED over-filtered 'the oldest properties we put UP FOR SALE' — a question about all listings — down to the approved ones.
